stem.text: The number of cars on a stretch of highway is modeled by \( W(t) = \ln{\left(t + 1 \right)} - 4 \sin{\left(\frac{t^{2}}{3} \right)} + 30 \) hundred cars, where t is measured in hours for \( 0 \le t \le 4 \). Using a calculator, find \( W'(2.5) \), the rate at which the amount is changing at time t = 2.5. Show the setup for the calculation, give the value correct to three decimal places, and include units.

worked_solution.text: The quantity asked for is the derivative of W at t = 2.5: \( W'(2.5) = \left. \frac{d}{dt}\left(\ln{\left(t + 1 \right)} - 4 \sin{\left(\frac{t^{2}}{3} \right)} + 30\right) \right|_{t=2.5} \).
With the calculator in radian mode, the numerical derivative at t = 2.5 gives \( W'(2.5) \) approximately 3.555 hundred cars per hour.

options.derivation: the derivative reported to two places instead of three
the function value W(2.5) reported in place of the derivative value
the numerical derivative taken with the calculator in degree mode, so the sine reads its argument in degrees
